groups.title: Cholesterol care: four different lives
groups.purpose: Explore medication concerns and shared decisions with four patients who have similar cholesterol findings and different life circumstances.
groups.differences: Ages 34–67; different self-described ethnicities, genders, education, work schedules, caregiving responsibilities and financial circumstances. Clinical findings, medication concerns, personality, communication style, disclosure gates and learning objectives are shared.
groups.provenance: Team-authored synthetic adaptations of supplied Omar Sinclair clinical material. Original source material is retained in each case.
groups.limitations: Exploratory comparison, not a controlled single-variable experiment. Four trials do not establish bias. Age and practical circumstances may appropriately change care; education must not be treated as a proxy for understanding. Order, repeated-case learning, model behavior and shared voice/portrait presentation are possible confounds. Faculty should assess each trial and review evidence before interpreting differences.
groups.sourceNote: Prepared before the demo. Source measurements retain their missing units and dates; no medications, allergies or imaging were invented. Independent clinical and bias calibration remains necessary.

sources.title: NHLBI: Blood cholesterol treatment
sources.excerpt: Selected teaching summary (paraphrase): Cholesterol treatment may include heart-healthy habits and medicines. Decisions should consider cholesterol levels, cardiovascular risk, other conditions, lifestyle, and the benefits and side effects of treatment. Patients and clinicians can work together on a suitable plan. Statins reduce cholesterol production in the liver and reduce heart attack and stroke risk in people with high LDL. Lifestyle advice includes limiting saturated fat and choosing whole grains, fruit and vegetables. This general teaching reference does not establish any particular patient's medication, understanding or treatment acceptance.

sources.title: AHA: Understanding blood pressure readings
sources.excerpt: Selected teaching summary (paraphrase): Blood pressure is recorded as systolic pressure during the heartbeat and diastolic pressure between beats, in mm Hg. Stage 2 is systolic at least 140 or diastolic at least 90. A health professional confirms a diagnosis. The AHA describes medication and lifestyle changes for stage 2 hypertension. Readings above 180 systolic and/or 120 diastolic require prompt attention; associated chest pain, breathlessness, neurologic symptoms or other listed emergency symptoms warrant emergency care. These general thresholds do not supply missing patient measurements, symptoms, dates or medications.
